violations.title: Food Contact Surface, Clean after Use
violations.observation: Equipment food-contact surfaces/utensils were not observed cleaned before any possible contamination. OBSERVED THE CUTTING EDGE OF THE CAN OPENER HAD BUILD UP OF DEBRIS.
violations.corrective_action: Equipment food-contact surfaces and utensils shall be cleaned at any time during the operation when contamination may have occurred. CFM REMOVED THE CAN OPENER FOR IT TO BE WASHED, RINSED, AND SANITIZED BEFORE NEXT USE.

violations.title: Non-TCS Food Contact Surface, Clean per Manufacturer
violations.observation: Enclosed components of ice bin are not being cleaned as required. OBSERVED MOLD-LIKE BUILD UP INSIDE THE ICE MACHINE OF THE SATELLITE KITCHEN.
violations.corrective_action: Surfaces of utensils and equipment contacting food that is NOT time/temperature control for safety food such as ice bins, beverage dispensing nozzles, and enclosed components of equipment such as ice makers, cooking oil storage tanks and distribution lines, beverage and syrup dispensing lines or tubes, coffee bean grinders, and water vending equipment at a frequency specified by the manufacturer or at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil or mold. CFM HAS REMOVED THE ICE MACHINE FROM SERVICE UNTIL IT CAN BE CLEANED.

out_items.name: Pasteurized foods used; prohibited foods not offered

violations.title: Pasteurized Food & Prohibited Food in HSP
violations.observation: The following unpasteurized prepackaged juice or unpasteurized prepackaged beverages containing juice is offered for sale or service in a facility serving a highly susceptible population: OBSERVED UNPASTEURIZED ORANGE JUICE IN THE REACH IN COOLER BY THE COOK LINE.
violations.corrective_action: In a food service establishment that serves a highly susceptible population (HSP) the following criteria applies to juice: 1) children in schools, day care settings, or similar facilities are included as HSP, 2) prepackaged juice or a prepackaged beverage containing juice that have not been specifically processed to prevent, reduce, or eliminate the presence of pathogens, or a packaged juice or beverage containing juice that bears a warning label may NOT be served or offered for sale, and 3) unpackaged juice that is prepared on the premises for service or sale in a ready-to-eat form shall be processed under a HACCP plan. CFM REMOVED THE UNPASTEURIZED ORANGE JUICE FROM THE KITCHEN AND MOVED THE PRODUCT TO AN EMPLOYEES ONLY LOCATION. EHS REQUESTS CFM TRAIN ALL STAFF MEMBERS IN CHARGE OF PURCHASING ON THE REQUIREMENT TO USE ONLY PASTEURIZED PACKAGED JUICE.

violations.corrective_action: Food shall be discarded if it: 1) exceeds 7 days or at 41F (except the time it is frozen); or 2) is in a container or package that does not bear a date or day. PIC DISCARDED THE FOOD.

violations.observation: Individually packaged ROP salmon filets were observed being stored over Ready-to-Eat food in the 1DR upright cooler in the main kitchen

out_items.name: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting

violations.title: Duty of PIC, Employee Health Policy in Place
violations.observation: Observed no signed employee health policy in place. Upon discussion, PIC states something similar is in the on-boarding.
violations.corrective_action: A complete employee health policy must have the following elements: 1) Employee training on foodborne illness, particularly symptoms of illness and prevention of the Big Six illnesses (see 'What is Foodborne Illness' handout); and 2) Documentation that employees have been instructed of their responsibility to report symptoms of, diagnosis of or exposure to foodborne illness to management (see 'Employee Illness Reporting Agreement' handout); and 3) A management plan to restrict or exclude employees, as applicable, who have symptoms, diagnosis or exposure to foodborne illness (see 'Employee Illness Decision Guide for PIC/CFM' handout). The information provided at the time of this inspection will help you develop and implement this policy. Handouts are available in the following languages: English, Arabic, Chinese (traditional), Farsi, Hindi, Korean, Spanish, Thai, Urdu and Vietnamese. If you have any questions about your employee health policy, please contact your area inspector or contact the Health Department at 703-246-2201, TTY 703-591-6435. EHS GAVE PIC THE FAIRFAX COUNTY’S “EMPLOYEE ILLNESS REPORTING AGREEMENT” TO PHOTOCOPY. EHS EMAILED PIC THE SPANISH VERSION OF THE SAME DOCUMENT. PLEASE HAVE ALL YOUR FOOD STAFF READ AND SIGN; RETAIN THESE DOCUMENTS FOR FUTURE ROUTINE INSPECTIONS.

out_items.name: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events

violations.title: Clean-up of vomiting and diarrheal events
violations.observation: The food establishment does not have written procedures for employees to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events. EHS observed no written procedures for vomit and diarrhea.
violations.corrective_action: A food establishment shall have written procedures for employees to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the food establishment. The procedures shall address the specific actions employees must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of employees, consumers, food and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter. EHS GAVE PIC A COPY OF FAIRFAX COUNTY’S VOMIT AND DIARRHEA CLEAN-UP POLICY.

violations.title: In-Use Utensils Proper Storage
violations.observation: EHS observed scoops with handles lying in bulk containers of panko, rice, and sugar with the handle touching the ingredient.
violations.corrective_action: During pauses in food preparation or dispensing, food utensils shall be stored in one of the following manners: 1) in the food with their handles above the top of the food and the container, 2) in food that is not time/temperature control for safety (TCS) food with their handles above the top of the food within containers or equipment that can be closed, 3) on a clean portion of the food preparation table or cooking equipment only if the in-use utensil and the food contact surface of the food preparation table or cooking equipment are cleaned and sanitized, 4) in running water of sufficient velocity to flush particulates to the drain, 5) in a clean, protected location if the utensils are used only with a food that is NOT TCS food, or 6) in a container of water if the water is maintained at a temperature of at least 135F and the container is cleaned frequently. EHS DISCUSSED WITH PIC ABOUT THE PROPER WAYS TO STORE SCOOPS WITH HANDLES. DO NOT USE BOWLS, CUPS, OR DELI CONTAINERS. SCOOPS WITH HANDLE CAN BE STORED INSIDE THE BULK CONTAINER WITH THE HANDLE STICKING UPWARDS.

violations.title: Equipment, Maintain in Good Repair/Condition
violations.observation: EHS observed the 1DR Supera glass display cooler in the satellite kitchen leaking water on the inside. A pool of water was found at the bottom of the unit.
violations.corrective_action: Equipment shall be maintained in a state of repair and condition that meets the requirements specified under Parts 4-1 and 4-2. EHS INSTRUCTED PIC TO TRANSFER ALL OF THE FOOD IN THAT UNIT TO A DIFFERENT COOLER. PIC INSTRUCTED MAINTENANCE TO SERVICE THE COOLER. PLEASE MAKE THIS CORRECTION BY THE NEXT ROUTINE INSPECTION.

violations.title: Hot Water Sanitizing Temperature Met
violations.observation: Due to improper operation of the hot water, mechanical warewashing machine upstairs, the dish simulating thermometer reached a maximum temperature of 149F, indicating that food-contact surfaces of equipment and utensils are not being adequately sanitized.
violations.corrective_action: Immediately discontinue use of the dishmachine. Repair the dishmachine so that a thermolabel will turn black. Until the machine is adequately repaired, set up the 3 vat sink to manually wash, rinse and chemically sanitize food-contact surfaces. The downstairs dish machine may also be used.
